title: Veterans property tax exemption
summary: Wyoming exempts $3,000 of assessed value a year on your principal residence. You need three years of Wyoming residency, and you can take it against your vehicle registration fees instead if that suits you better.
amount: An annual exemption of $3,000 of assessed value
eligibility: You are a bona fide Wyoming resident, and have been for at least three years at the time you claim
An honorably discharged Veteran of the Indian Wars, Spanish American War, Filipino insurrection, Boxer rebellion, Puerto Rico campaign or First World War
Or of the Second World War, serving between 7 December 1941 and 31 December 1946
Or of the Korean War emergency, serving between 27 June 1950 and 31 January 1955
Or of the Vietnam War emergency, serving between 28 February 1961 and 7 May 1975
Or an honorably discharged Veteran awarded the armed forces expeditionary medal or another authorized service or campaign medal indicating service in any armed conflict in a foreign country
Or a disabled Veteran with a compensable service-connected disability certified by the Veterans Administration or a branch of the armed forces
A surviving spouse, during widowhood or widowerhood, of anyone qualifying above or who died while serving honorably during a qualifying period
details: File a sworn claim with your county assessor on or before the fourth Monday in May. The exemption applies to your principal residence only, and you may claim it in only one Wyoming county.

Missing the deadline is not fatal and the rule is unusually generous. An honorably discharged claimant who files late still receives the exemption for that taxable year, in addition to the following year's, provided they file by the fourth Monday in May of the next year.

After your first sworn claim you do not have to file again. In later years you simply contact the assessor's office by telephone, mail or another method on or before the fourth Monday in May and confirm you still qualify.

There is a useful alternative. Under subsection (g) you may file after the deadline and still get the benefit for that year, but only applied to reduce motor vehicle registration fees. If you do not own your home, or the property exemption is not useful to you, ask about that route.
The exemption covers property held in a trust created by or for your benefit, and property you are buying under a recorded contract for deed, not just property held outright.

A surviving spouse qualifies in their own right if both spouses were Wyoming residents at the time of death, the surviving spouse has been a Wyoming resident for at least three years when claiming, and the Veteran would have qualified had they survived and applied.
The county assessor must notify taxpayers of this exemption with the annual assessment schedule, including instructions and timelines.
The $3,000 is fixed in the statute with no inflation adjustment. Wyoming has no state income tax, so there is no military retirement question here.
statuteRef: Wyo. Stat. 39-13-105, with the exemption authorised by 39-11-105(a)(xxiv)
